catalog.summary: Picks one option from a popup list.

patternStatus: Three pages answer this family. The combobox pattern owns the control, its role and its properties; the select-only combobox example owns the key table, because a combobox that takes no text is what this family is; the listbox pattern owns the popup, its options, its groups and its selection states. All three were read on 2026-09-04 and transcribed

searchRoles.reason: The combobox pattern lists the four roles a popup may carry — listbox, tree, grid, dialog — and says that a popup with any role but listbox is named by aria-haspopup on the control. A popup holding a text field and a list is a dialog, so with search the content carries role=dialog, the trigger writes aria-haspopup="dialog", and the listbox moves one element in onto the list part. Without search nothing moves and the content is the listbox it has always been.

nativeElement.reason: A native select cannot hold an option with an icon, a description or a check mark; it cannot be styled past its closed state in any browser; and its popup is drawn by the operating system, so it answers no density, no color scheme and no direction. The cost of refusing it is the whole key table, the whole popup, and a visually hidden native select carried alongside so a plain form still submits and reset() still restores.

collection.reason: moveIndex, because the highlight is aria-activedescendant rather than DOM focus and packages/core/src/focus/arrow-navigation moves real focus. createFilter and matchRanges, because docs/component-features.md §2.9 asks that search compare the way the reader's locale compares and §6 refuses an assumed contains — combobox is the consumer, and select shares the module for movement alone.

portalledIdentity.reason: The family is two subtrees: the control, where the consumer wrote it, and the popup, portalled to the end of the document. A stylesheet has no way to reach a subtree that is no longer inside the root, so data-ui is written on both. menu did not face this — its layer is its root and its trigger belongs to the consumer — and popover, tooltip and dialog each declined a trigger part for the same reason. A consumer's [data-ui='select'] selector therefore matches the control and the popup, and both rows are in the anatomy table.

branches: the control root, so pressing the trigger again closes rather than dismissing twice
layer.reason: One layer in the single stack, at the token popover and menu already use: an anchored surface above the page and below a toast. Modality is declined to dialog, as popover and menu both declined it, because inerting the page would inert the control that has to close the popup.

highlight.focus: stays on the trigger for the whole interaction
highlight.reason: The APG's own select-only example keeps DOM focus on the combobox and marks the option with aria-activedescendant, and combobox — this family's pair — has no choice, because its input must keep focus for the reader to type. One model across both is what lets data-current and aria-selected mean the same thing in both popups. The cost is that focus/arrow-navigation cannot be used and the family binds its own keys.

busy.reason: While an answer is travelling the control shows the ring instead of the chevron: the chevron says the popup opens, and it does not open onto anything yet. The ring is the one B4 drew once for every family (spinner/spinner.css) rather than a second arc drawn here, and this family only says where it stands and how big it is.

placeholder.reason: The popup waits as three rows the height of an option rather than as one sentence, so the surface a reader is looking at is the shape of the list that is coming. It is hidden from assistive technology: the status row beside it is the live region and already says what is happening (SL6/CB5).

chips.reason: Several chosen values are the chips themselves rather than a sentence about them (SL4/CB4). Each chip is a `tag`, worn as `data-ui` beside the row this family owns, so the chip a reader removes here is the chip they know from everywhere else and its geometry is stated once. What does not fit collapses into one chip marked `data-overflow`, measured by `createCollapse` — the same ResizeObserver arithmetic `toolbar` collapses a bar with. Under 120px of control there is no room for a chip at all, and the summary sentence answers instead; the swap is a container query, so it costs no observer and no render.
chips.bandReason: The control holds one line, so a reader who chose twelve values sees three chips and a count. The band at the top of the popup holds all of them, wraps, and scrolls at about two rows of its own — so what is chosen stays legible without the control growing and without a `+N` standing in front of it (SL10). It is drawn only while something is chosen. Its chips carry no remove control, and the reason is keyboard reach rather than tidiness. Without `search` focus never enters this layer at all, so a widget in there would be a tab stop the pattern excludes and a control nothing could reach. With `search` focus does enter it — and the layer's one `Tab` is spent commiting and leaving the control, so a remove control in the band would be reachable by pointer and by nothing else, which is the parity failure the first reason was protecting against. Restated rather than dropped (SL11). Taking a value back is the option's own row, which the list has open beside it and which a query can hide until `Escape` clears it, and the chips in the control, which are focusable.

wiring.role: combobox on the trigger, listbox on the content, option on each item
wiring.aria-haspopup: listbox, on the trigger. Redundant for role=combobox, whose implicit value is listbox, and written anyway because the element is a button and role=combobox replaces button on it. With search it is dialog, which the pattern requires of a popup that is not a listbox.
wiring.aria-autocomplete: list, on the search input. The list under it is filtered by what was typed, which is what the value names.
wiring.aria-expanded: true while the popup is open, false while it is closed, always written
wiring.aria-controls: the trigger names the content while the popup is open
wiring.aria-activedescendant: the trigger names the highlighted option, and nothing while there is none. With search it is the search input that names it, because that is the element holding focus.
wiring.aria-selected: true on every committed option, false on every other selectable one, which is what the listbox pattern requires
wiring.aria-multiselectable: true on the content when multiple is set
wiring.id: inside a field the trigger carries the field's control identifier (field › wiring.id), so the label's for names it and a press on the label focuses it: a button is labelable content in HTML. Outside a field the identifier is generated.
wiring.aria-labelledby: the trigger also takes the field's label, because the name a label element gives a button is not reliably carried to a button whose role is combobox
wiring.aria-describedby: the trigger takes the field's description and error
wiring.aria-disabled: never written. The trigger is a real button and carries the native attribute, which a disabled fieldset can also set on its own.
wiring.aria-readonly: on the trigger, because neither a button nor role=combobox has a readonly the platform enforces
wiring.aria-required: on the trigger, from the prop or from the field
wiring.aria-invalid: on the trigger, from the prop or from the field
wiring.aria-setsize: on each option when total is given, which is what an incrementally loaded list sets
wiring.aria-posinset: beside aria-setsize, for the same reason
wiring.aria-modal: never written. The page behind the popup is still there and still reachable.

keyboard.effect: closed, opens the popup onto the selected option or the first; open, moves the highlight to the next option, wrapping only when loop is true
keyboard.focus: stays on the trigger; the highlight moves and aria-activedescendant follows it

keyboard.effect: closed, opens the popup onto the last option; open, moves the highlight to the previous option. The example opens onto the first; the last is the mirror of ArrowDown and what every surveyed implementation does, and the departure is recorded in the design.
opens the popup without moving the highlight
commits the highlighted option and closes
closed, opens; open, commits the highlighted option and closes
closed, opens; open and single, commits and closes; open and multiple, toggles the highlighted option and keeps the popup open, which is the listbox pattern's recommended multiple-selection model
opens if closed, and highlights the first option
opens if closed, and highlights the last option
moves the highlight ten options on, or to the last, and never wraps
moves the highlight ten options back, or to the first, and never wraps
opens if closed, and highlights the first option whose label begins with the sequence typed; the same character repeated cycles through the options beginning with it
commits the highlighted option, closes, and moves on. The example states this and notes it differs from a native select, which closes and does not move.
keyboard.focus: the next element in the page

searchKeyboard.effect: moves the highlight to the next option, wrapping only when loop is true
moves the highlight to the previous option
moves the highlight ten options on, or to the last
moves the highlight ten options back, or to the first
the browser's caret movement. Not bound, where the closed control binds it to the first option: the pattern's editable branch returns Home to the caret, and combobox answers the same way.
the browser's caret movement. Not bound, for the reason Home is not.
commits the highlighted option, and closes unless multiple keeps the popup open
searchKeyboard.focus: the trigger after closing, the search input otherwise

searchKeyboard.effect: types a space into the query. Not bound, where the closed control binds it to a commit: a field the reader is typing into cannot spend the space bar.
a non-empty query is cleared and the popup stays; an empty query closes the popup. The pattern names the clearing branch and makes it optional.
searchKeyboard.focus: the search input, then the trigger once the popup closes

searchKeyboard.effect: commits the highlighted option, closes, and moves on — the same effect the closed control's Tab has. Focus is inside a portalled layer at the end of the document, so the browser's own next element is not the element after the control; the family reads the document's tab order with tabbables() from @slotted/core/focus, finds the trigger in it and moves to the entry beside it. Shift+Tab moves to the entry before it.
searchKeyboard.focus: the element after the control, or the element before it under Shift

searchKeyboard.effect: typed into the query. Never intercepted, and typeahead is off while search is on.

focus.onOpen: nothing moves; the trigger keeps focus and the highlight goes to the selected option, or to the first
focus.onOpenSearching: the search input takes focus, however the popup was opened — a press on the trigger included. The combobox pattern's own note says a dialog popup does not support aria-activedescendant and that DOM focus moves into the dialog.
focus.restoreSearching: the trigger takes focus back when the popup closes by escape, by a commit or by any key. It does not on an outside press or a blur: the reader has just put focus somewhere themselves, and a control that took it back would undo the gesture that closed it.
focus.restore: never leaves the trigger, so there is nothing to restore
focus.disabledItems: A disabled option is announced with aria-disabled, carries data-disabled, keeps its place in the collection and is skipped by every movement key. It cannot be committed.
focus.guardsReason: popover needs two focus guards because Tab inside a non-modal portalled layer has nowhere to go. Focus never enters this layer, so there is nothing inside it for Tab to reach. With search there is exactly one focusable element in it and Tab is bound to commit, close and place focus beside the trigger in the document's own tab order, so a guard would have nothing to catch.
focus.removal: The option holding the highlight cannot be removed while it holds focus, because it never holds focus. When the collection loses the highlighted option the highlight falls back to the selected option, then to the first, then to nothing.

typeahead.label: the item's textValue, or its label part's text
typeahead.locale: Intl.Collator at base sensitivity, so Ä matches a
typeahead.reason: The listbox pattern recommends it for every listbox and especially above seven options, and the select-only example ships it. menu recorded listbox as the module's next consumer; this family is the one that arrived first.
typeahead.disabledBy: search, because a reader typing into a field cannot also be driving a typeahead on the same keys

search.filter: createFilter from @slotted/core/collection, replaced by the filter prop and turned off by filter={null}
search.highlight: the highlight family inside the label part, handed the query and the locale the filter used
search.focus: moves to the search input as the popup opens and returns to the trigger as it closes, because the combobox pattern says a dialog popup does not support aria-activedescendant and DOM focus moves into it
search.tabOrder: tabbables() from @slotted/core/focus, read over the document with the layer's own subtree excluded, so Tab leaves the control for the element beside it rather than for the end of the document
search.query: transient. It is emptied when an option is committed and when the popup closes, it never becomes a value, and no request carries both it and the selection.
search.reason: Seven of the twelve implementations surveyed on 2026-09-08 ship a search on the select itself, and the five that decline each publish a combobox and route the reader there. This library publishes that combobox too, and it is the family whose typed text is a contract: inputValue, allowsCustomValue and aria-autocomplete. A reader choosing one of two hundred known offices is not authoring a value. Putting the field inside the popup is what keeps docs/component-features.md §6's promise that the control takes no typed text, and what keeps the two families distinguishable at a glance.

overflow.reason: The same bound menu takes, for the same reason: Radix, Base UI and React Aria each publish the remaining height and none of them bounds itself, so a list of a hundred options runs off the bottom of the screen.

measure.value: the content's own width by default, never narrower than the anchor's width and capped by the measure and the available width; exactly the anchor's width when width is anchor
measure.reason: A popup pinned to the control's width wraps its option labels under a narrow control: a filter-bar select of 120 pixels breaks "Paused · 1" over two lines. The control's width is the floor, so the popup never reads as a second, smaller control. width="anchor" pins it to the control's width exactly.

value.reason: Every surveyed implementation paints the placeholder when a controlled value matches no option, which is what an async list shows on its first render while it still holds a value. The value part renders the consumer's own function instead, and data-unmatched says the label could not be resolved, so a form never looks empty while holding a value.

form.react: a visually hidden native select carrying name, required, form and one option per value
form.reason: Neither ecosystem has the other's mechanism. The hidden select is what makes a plain form submit, a native reset() restore and a browser's own validation bubble point at the right control; Radix ships the same element for the same reason. The asymmetry is recorded rather than levelling both to the smaller shape.

mount.active: the layer exists only while it is open
mount.lazy: built on the first open and kept afterwards
mount.reason: The same axis tooltip, popover, collapsible and menu declare.

motion.reason: The popup grows from the control that opened it, which is what says where it came from. The same grammar tooltip, popover and menu use, so four anchored layers do not open four different ways.

positioning.reason: The popup hangs from the start edge of the control and is never narrower than it, so the value in the control and the labels in the list share one edge. The offset is four rather than menu's zero: a menu's gap is its layer's own padding, needed so a pointer travelling into a submenu never crosses page, and this family has no submenu and no grace area to protect.

itemAligned.reason: Radix ships position="item-aligned" and makes it the default, and Material has disableOptionCentering for the same behavior; Radix's own examples set position="popper". It scrolls and offsets the popup so the selected option lands under the pointer, which needs a measured scroll on every open, cannot survive a bounded height, and is a macOS convention rather than a web one. No composition replaces it, and the cost is recorded rather than hidden.

modal.reason: Base UI defaults its select to modal. docs/component-features.md §8 gives the modal surface to Dialog, and popover and menu each declined it there. applyInert in dismissable-layer inerts everything outside the layer, the control included, so a modal select could not be closed by pressing the control again.

backdrop.reason: Base UI ships Select.Backdrop. A backdrop darkens the page behind a modal and catches the press that closes it; modality is declined above and the press outside already belongs to the dismissable layer.

arrow.reason: Base UI and Ark both ship an arrow on a select. The popup is never narrower than its control and hangs directly under it, so the control already says where it came from; the anchored surface that points at something is popover. Declining it is also what frees the part name arrow for the chevron on the trigger.

chips.reason: docs/component-features.md §6 files removable chips, creation, limits, duplicates, reorder and paste under MultiSelect / Tags Input, which is wave 6 item 5. This family ships multiple with a summary in the trigger — the same paragraph asks for "resumo" — and a consumer who needs chips reaches for the family that owns them.

freeText.reason: docs/component-features.md §6 ends the Select paragraph with it: "Does not include free-text input. Large volume or explicit search uses Combobox." The two families ship together for that reason.

virtualization.reason: docs/component-features.md §2.10 makes virtualization a capability of the collection engine rather than a parallel component, and menu deferred it there. A bounded, scrolling popup plus typeahead, Home, End and the page keys hold a hundred options, which the harness proves.

debounce.reason: Not applicable to a family with no query, and declined for combobox in the same session: a debounce belongs to the consumer's fetch, and a family that delayed its own request would delay a controlled consumer's re-render and drop characters.
